reason: The drum and its bearing bracket need a firm mounting on the crane before it can wind a lifting cord.
expectation: The winding drum will be mounted on the crane frame.

alternatives.reason: The crank may need to be fitted to the drum before it is mounted.

effect: The crank had to be fitted to the drum first, producing a hand winch ready to mount.
reaction: The explanation of the longer crank's trade-off was useful; I had guessed the mounting order incorrectly.
reason: The assembled winch now needs a place on the crane to wind the lifting cord.
expectation: The hand winch will be mounted on the crane.

effect: The hand winch is mounted, so the crane can now be fitted with its lifting cord.
reason: The cord needs to connect the winch to the crane's tip pulley and hook.
expectation: The cord and hook will be fitted to the crane for lifting.

effect: The lifting line is fitted, leaving the crane ready for its holding and stability equipment.
reaction: The cord fitting worked as expected.
reason: The pawl and release lever should let the winch hold a raised load and release it for lowering.
expectation: The holding mechanism will be fitted to the crane.

alternatives.reason: The crane may need ballast before its holding mechanism is fitted.

effect: The pawl is fitted to hold the drum, but the crane still needs protection against tipping.
reaction: The distinction between holding the rope and stabilizing the crane is useful.
reason: Rear ballast should help balance the crane before testing a load.
expectation: The ballast will be fitted to the rear of the crane to help resist tipping.

effect: The ballast is fitted, and the crane is ready for a low test of both stability and the holding pawl.
reaction: Testing the two mechanisms together makes sense.
reason: The small padded test weight is suited to the low test before lifting the cargo basket.

choice.with: Ballasted holding crane ready for a test

expectation: The crane will lift and hold the test weight so its stability and pawl can be checked.

effect: The low test confirmed that the ballasted crane stays grounded and the pawl holds the drum; the crank must be held while releasing it to lower a load.
reaction: The test made the separate roles of the ballast and pawl clear.
reason: The tested crane can now try lifting the cargo basket to complete the goal.
expectation: The crane will lift, hold, and gently lower the basket.

effect: The basket lift, hold and controlled lowering completed the crane goal, confirming the tested setup worked with its intended load.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the pawl and release used in a complete delivery.

mostWorthwhile.text: The low test made the ballast and pawl's different jobs clear, and explained how to lower safely. That mechanism was worth the player's time.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the assembled winch was straightforward but less informative than the later test.

surprise.text: I initially expected to mount the drum first; the feedback showed that the crank and drum had to become a hand winch before mounting.

arbitrary.text: The required assembly order was not obvious at first, though the compatibility feedback resolved it immediately.

continue.text: Yes. The practical explanations and testing of the crane made me curious about what the fair will do next, even though some assembly steps were predictable.
